findings.text: The first lines tell a newcomer what Athena is and how it differs from other tools. This is the only description of Athena itself; the rest of the page is about a different project.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The header explains why the page exists and why it matters: it shows Athena's output. The claim links go to exact file lines at a pinned commit, so a reader can check that the evidence is real.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: Someone arriving at Athena's site does not know what firstmate is, and the title does not say. Firstmate is first explained in the 'Start here' section, below three lede paragraphs.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The 'Start here' section works well as an on-ramp. It gives a one-sentence definition of firstmate, defines terms before they are used, and has short sections on what firstmate is, one piece of work from start to finish, and what can go wrong. A reader who stops here still learns the essentials.

The next steps are concrete and easy to find, and the header links to them. But the install step assumes the reader already has a checkout. It gives no clone command and no prerequisites, although the page says Athena is written in Rust.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The deeper cards use terms the Glossary does not define, such as endpoint, pin (in the harness sense), durable record and captain-held inventory. A newcomer reading past 'Start here' loses the thread.
findings.source: t8 card: "a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead"; t11: "its captain-held inventory is verified"

findings.text: Some Glossary entries are circular or weak. 'Wake' itself is never defined, and the 'ship' entry says little more than that ships are mentioned next to scouts.
findings.source: Glossary: "stale wake — A wake after which the agent inspects a worker..."; "ship — A kind of task, named next to scouts."

findings.text: The page openly says what its sources do not support, which builds trust. However, the same yolo/in-scope caveat appears about six times, which makes a long page longer.
findings.source: "in scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: This mentions a 'studies/' folder without saying which repository it is in. A newcomer cannot follow it without first finding the Athena repository.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
